summary: A Depth subscription on an NFO future with OI: V2 ticks with the five-level book, an update of both sides, then sides Firstock marks invalid (a sentinel level among valid ones, a side of sentinels, a side of zero levels), then a valid book again.

notes: Depth mode's OI is i_total_open_interest on both (firstock_adapter.py:862; brokers/firstock/streaming.rs tick).

Firstock has no book-clear signal the web acts on: a level whose price, quantity or orders is 9223372036854775808, or with neither price nor quantity, is dropped, and a side left without a valid level keeps the previous side (firstock_adapter.py:683-744). Audit FB-02, still open: the desktop replaces the side with whatever array came (brokers/firstock/streaming.rs merge, levels), so a sentinel or zero level is published as a zero level and a sentinel between valid levels pushes the next valid level down.

deviations.reason: data.mode is the label every broker's frames carry on the desktop (ltp, quote, full), as the recorded Zerodha transcripts carry it; this web adapter puts its subscription mode number there.

Firstock's i_last_trade_time is in epoch seconds and the web sends it unchanged as ltt; feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop sends the trade time in ms.
The desktop sends OI as both oi and open_interest for every broker, as the recorded Zerodha transcript does; this web adapter sends oi only.

The desktop's Depth frame carries every Quote field of the instrument's latest tick (one Depth schema for every broker, docs/api/websocket-streaming/depth.md lists the trade quantity and book totals); this web adapter's Depth dict leaves out last_quantity although Firstock's tick carries it.

Audit FB-02: the web drops levels Firstock marks invalid (the 9223372036854775808 sentinel in price, quantity or orders, or neither price nor quantity) and keeps the previous side when none is valid; the desktop publishes them as zero levels.
The web sends Firstock's circuit limits (i_upper_circuit_limit, i_lower_circuit_limit, /100); the desktop's common carrier drops them.
